Bearer-Auth.description:
The App API uses a bearer authentication scheme.

You can generate a bearer token, known as an **App API Key**, with a defined scope in [your account settings](https://fly.customer.io/settings/api_credentials?keyType=app). [Learn more about bearer authorization in Customer.io](/accounts/settings/managing-credentials).

ServiceAccount-Auth.description:
Transactional send endpoints (`/v1/send/email`, `/v1/send/push`, `/v1/send/sms`, `/v1/send/whatsapp`, `/v1/send/in_app`, `/v1/send/inbox_message`) also accept a service-account bearer token, prefixed with `sa_live_`. Service-account tokens work across workspaces, so you must pass the target workspace as the `X-Workspace-Id` header on each request.

Service-account tokens are intended for testing and one-off sends—for example, using the Customer.io CLI with an AI agent like Claude to verify that a transactional message renders correctly before wiring it into your production backend. **For the production integration that triggers the message from your application, use an App API Key instead**: it's workspace-scoped, easier to rotate, and has a smaller blast radius.

Service-account tokens are server-side credentials. Treat them like any API key—keep them in environment variables or a secret manager, and never embed them in client-side code, mobile apps, or other untrusted contexts.

ServiceAccount-Auth.description:
Transactional send endpoints (`/v1/send/email`, `/v1/send/push`, `/v1/send/sms`, `/v1/send/whatsapp`, `/v1/send/in_app`, `/v1/send/inbox_message`) also accept a service-account bearer token, prefixed with `sa_live_`. Service-account tokens work across workspaces, so you must pass the target workspace as the `X-Workspace-Id` header on each request.

Service-account tokens are intended for testing and one-off sends—for example, using the Customer.io CLI with an AI agent like Claude to verify that a transactional message renders correctly before wiring it into your production backend. **For the production integration that triggers the message from your application, use an App API Key instead**: it's workspace-scoped, easier to rotate, and has a smaller blast radius.

Service-account tokens are server-side credentials. Treat them like any API key—keep them in environment variables or a secret manager, and never embed them in client-side code, mobile apps, or other untrusted contexts.

The content or its destination can't be published as-is. Possible reasons:
  - The content has Liquid errors. The `meta` object lists them per language.
  - The destination won't accept content because it's archived, stopping, or being deleted.

  - The language group is over the limit of 50 variants.

add_title_to_head.description: Add a `<title>` tag to `<head>` using the email subject line (creates or replaces if empty).

add_vml_alt_text.description: Add `alt` attribute to VML elements (used by Outlook’s Word rendering engine), derived from the element’s text content.

language.description: Language code (for example, `"en"`, `"fr"`, or `"ar"`) used for `lang` and `dir` attributes.

remove_button_role_from_links.description: Remove `role="button"` from `<a>` tags to restore proper link semantics for screen readers.

remove_zoom_meta_tag.description: Remove viewport `<meta>` tags that restrict zoom (`user-scalable=0`, `user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`, or `maximum-scale=2`).

css_inliner.description: Moves CSS from `<style>` tags into inline `style` attributes on each element. Essential for email clients with limited `<style>` support (for example, older Gmail and some Outlook versions). Uses the `juice` library. Elements in `<style>` tags marked with `data-ignore-inlining` are skipped.

apply_html_attributes.description: Controls adding redundant HTML attributes alongside inlined CSS to different HTML elements.

apply_height_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `height` attributes alongside inlined CSS `height` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS height.

apply_table_element_attributes.description: Add redundant HTML attributes on table elements (`<table>`, `<th>`, `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<caption>`, `<colgroup>`, `<col>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`): `background-color` → `bgcolor`, `background-image` → `background`, `text-align` → `align`, `vertical-align` → `valign`.

apply_width_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `width` attributes alongside inlined CSS `width` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS width (for example, older Outlook).

preserve_pseudos.description: Keep pseudo-selector rules (for example, `:hover`) in `<style>` (cannot be inlined).

remove_style_tags.description: Remove `<style>` tags after inlining their rules.

css_variables.description: Resolves CSS custom properties (`var(--name)`) into their computed values. Required for email clients that do not support CSS custom properties (most email clients). Variables declared in one `<style>` tag are available in subsequent `<style>` tags.

preserve.description: Keep original custom property declarations (`--name: value`) alongside the resolved values.

encode_entities.description: Encodes special characters (for example, `©`, `™`, and `—`) as their HTML entity equivalents. Improves rendering consistency across email clients with varying character encoding support. Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags and avoids double-encoding existing entities.

formatter.description: Controls the output formatting of the final HTML. Only one mode (`prettify` or `minify`) can be active at a time. Set to `"none"` to skip formatting entirely.

minify.description: Options used when `type` is `"minify"`. Reduces file size by stripping whitespace and comments.

line_length_limit.description: Maximum characters per line before inserting a line break.

remove_html_comments.description: HTML comment removal level. `"0"` keeps all comments, `"1"` removes non-conditional comments (preserves MSO conditionals like `<!--[if mso]>`), and `"2"` removes all comments including conditional.

remove_line_breaks.description: Remove all line breaks from the output.

prettify.description: Options used when `type` is `"prettify"`. Produces human-readable, indented HTML output.

indent_size.description: Number of indent characters per level.

wrap_attributes.description: Wrap HTML attributes onto separate lines (`force-expand-multiline` mode).

prevent_widows.description: Replaces the last space in text blocks with a non-breaking space (` `) to prevent a single word from wrapping onto its own line (a “widow”). remove_unused_css.description: Scans the HTML and removes any CSS selectors from `<style>` tags that are not referenced in the document. uglify.description: Shorten (uglify) CSS class names to reduce file size.

transformers.description: Automate repetitive actions like removing white space and inlining CSS with [transformers](/journeys/design-studio/emails/code-editor/overview/#transformers).

accessibility.description: Applies a set of accessibility improvements to the email HTML. When no `language` is set, this falls back to the `lang` attribute on the `<html>` tag, or `"und"` (undetermined). The `dir` attribute is automatically derived from the language using RTL detection.

add_dir_to_content.description: Add `dir` attribute to direct children of `<body>`.

add_dir_to_html.description: Add `dir` attribute (`ltr`, `rtl`, or `auto`) to the `<html>` element if not already present.

add_empty_alt_to_images.description: Add `alt=""` to `` elements missing an `alt` attribute, preventing screen readers from reading the file name.

add_lang_to_content.description: Add `lang` attribute to direct children of `<body>`.

add_lang_to_html.description: Add `lang` attribute to the `<html>` element if not already present.

add_role_to_tables.description: Add `role="presentation"` to all `<table>` elements without an existing `role`, so screen readers skip table semantics for layout tables.

add_title_to_head.description: Add a `<title>` tag to `<head>` using the email subject line (creates or replaces if empty).

add_vml_alt_text.description: Add `alt` attribute to VML elements (used by Outlook’s Word rendering engine), derived from the element’s text content.

language.description: Language code (for example, `"en"`, `"fr"`, or `"ar"`) used for `lang` and `dir` attributes.

remove_button_role_from_links.description: Remove `role="button"` from `<a>` tags to restore proper link semantics for screen readers.

remove_zoom_meta_tag.description: Remove viewport `<meta>` tags that restrict zoom (`user-scalable=0`, `user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`, or `maximum-scale=2`).

css_inliner.description: Moves CSS from `<style>` tags into inline `style` attributes on each element. Essential for email clients with limited `<style>` support (for example, older Gmail and some Outlook versions). Uses the `juice` library. Elements in `<style>` tags marked with `data-ignore-inlining` are skipped.

apply_html_attributes.description: Controls adding redundant HTML attributes alongside inlined CSS to different HTML elements.

apply_height_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `height` attributes alongside inlined CSS `height` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS height.

apply_table_element_attributes.description: Add redundant HTML attributes on table elements (`<table>`, `<th>`, `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<caption>`, `<colgroup>`, `<col>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>`): `background-color` → `bgcolor`, `background-image` → `background`, `text-align` → `align`, `vertical-align` → `valign`.

apply_width_attributes.description:
Add redundant HTML `width` attributes alongside inlined CSS `width` on ``, `
`, ``, and `` elements. Only applies to `px` values (and `%` on table elements). Needed for email clients that ignore CSS width (for example, older Outlook).

preserve_pseudos.description: Keep pseudo-selector rules (for example, `:hover`) in `<style>` (cannot be inlined).

remove_style_tags.description: Remove `<style>` tags after inlining their rules.

css_variables.description: Resolves CSS custom properties (`var(--name)`) into their computed values. Required for email clients that do not support CSS custom properties (most email clients). Variables declared in one `<style>` tag are available in subsequent `<style>` tags.

preserve.description: Keep original custom property declarations (`--name: value`) alongside the resolved values.

encode_entities.description: Encodes special characters (for example, `©`, `™`, and `—`) as their HTML entity equivalents. Improves rendering consistency across email clients with varying character encoding support. Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags and avoids double-encoding existing entities.

formatter.description: Controls the output formatting of the final HTML. Only one mode (`prettify` or `minify`) can be active at a time. Set to `"none"` to skip formatting entirely.

minify.description: Options used when `type` is `"minify"`. Reduces file size by stripping whitespace and comments.

line_length_limit.description: Maximum characters per line before inserting a line break.

remove_html_comments.description: HTML comment removal level. `"0"` keeps all comments, `"1"` removes non-conditional comments (preserves MSO conditionals like `<!--[if mso]>`), and `"2"` removes all comments including conditional.

remove_line_breaks.description: Remove all line breaks from the output.

prettify.description: Options used when `type` is `"prettify"`. Produces human-readable, indented HTML output.

indent_size.description: Number of indent characters per level.

wrap_attributes.description: Wrap HTML attributes onto separate lines (`force-expand-multiline` mode).

prevent_widows.description: Replaces the last space in text blocks with a non-breaking space (` `) to prevent a single word from wrapping onto its own line (a “widow”). Only processes text nodes in the `<body>` and skips `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<svg>`, and `<head>` elements. Preserves Liquid template tags (`{{ }} ` and `{% %}`).

remove_unused_css.description: Scans the HTML and removes any CSS selectors from `<style>` tags that are not referenced in the document. Reduces file size and helps avoid Gmail’s 102 KB clipping limit. HTML and CSS comments are always preserved by this step (comment removal is handled separately by the formatter object).

backend_markers.description: Template syntax delimiters (e.g., Liquid, Handlebars) that the CSS parser should skip over to avoid treating template expressions as invalid CSS.

uglify.description: Shorten (uglify) CSS class names to reduce file size.

whitelist.description:

  - .ReadMsgBody

items.description: A CSS selector to always keep.

type.description:
Why this device has no screenshot:
  - `bounced`: the vendor rendered the device and reported a bounce.
  - `vendor_timeout`: submitted to the vendor, but didn't finish in time.
  - `client_rejected`: the vendor refused the device id.
  - `vendor_request`: the submission to the vendor itself failed.
  - `abandoned`: submitted, but the outcome is unknown.
  - `expired`: the screenshot rendered successfully but has since aged out of its retention window and is no longer available. Unlike the other types, this isn't a render failure.
  - `other`: any other cause.

A tile with any of these types (except `expired`) was refunded its credit.

full_thumbnail.description: Capture URL for a reduced, full-length version of the default screenshot. Omitted unless the render completed.

os.description: Operating system the client runs on.

screenshots.description: Capture URLs keyed by image name—the full-size screenshot under `default`, plus a key per extra image the device renders. This is the only place the full-size URL appears; `thumbnail` and `full_thumbnail` are reduced variants. Omitted unless the render completed.

status.description: The vendor's own status for this device's render. Only `Complete` and `Bounced` are terminal.

thumbnail.description: Capture URL for a reduced-size version of the default screenshot. Useful for grid/list views where you don't want to load full-size screenshots. Omitted unless the render completed.

total_previews_bounced.description: Previews that produced no screenshot, whether the vendor bounced them or they failed on Customer.io's side. Their credits are refunded when the run settles.

total_previews_cached.description: Previews served from an earlier run's screenshot. Not charged, and not counted in `total_previews_succeeded`.

total_previews_ready.description: How many previews show a screenshot you can fetch, counted from the tiles themselves. This is the progress count to compare against `total_previews_requested`—`total_previews_succeeded` alone reads `0` on a fully cached run. It isn't the completion signal; `is_processed` is. Because a tile can be served by an earlier screenshot of the same content while this run's own render is still in flight, this can reach `total_previews_requested` before the run finishes.

total_previews_requested.description: Previews requested in the job, for the email in the path. On a settled run, this is normally `total_previews_cached` + `total_previews_succeeded` + `total_previews_bounced`.

total_previews_succeeded.description: Previews this run generated itself, excluding cached ones. A fully cached run reports `0` here even though every tile is `Complete`—compare `total_previews_ready` against `total_previews_requested` instead to track progress.

updated_at.description: When the job's status was last updated.
